MA342 overview

MA342 Topic Guide

Secondary Applications

Separate the now-current connectedness/IVT bridge from genuinely older application material.

Purpose

Prepare the Intermediate Value Theorem as a current connectedness application, while retaining Euler/triangulation, Brouwer, FTA and Nash-style questions at lower priority.Exam use: The 2025/26 Q4(b) directly asks for the continuous-image theorem and its IVT consequence for 6 marks; the older application families are absent from the latest three papers.

Question plan

  1. Identify whether the question asks for a current connectedness application or an older named theorem.
  2. State the theorem and check its hypotheses in the concrete setting.
  3. For IVT, identify the connected interval, the continuous map and why its image contains every intermediate real value.
  4. Question interpretation: “Explain how the preceding part implies IVT” means apply the connected-image result, not re-prove IVT by supremum arguments.

Definitions

Current bridge: a continuous image of a connected space is connected, and connected subsets of R are intervals. This yields IVT because h([a,b]) is a connected subset of R containing h(a) and h(b). Older material: for a suitable finite triangulation, χ=V−E+F; Brouwer says every continuous self-map of a closed ball has a fixed point; the topological FTA proof uses global properties of maps on C.Rapid recall: IVT is now core evidence; Euler, Brouwer, FTA and Nash remain archive-led secondary material.

Proof method

For IVT, use that [a,b] is connected, continuity makes h([a,b]) connected, and connected subsets of R are intervals. For older theorem applications, explicitly map the data to each hypothesis before drawing the conclusion.Exam workflow: Name the source space, preservation theorem and target-space classification, then state the requested consequence.

Worked simple example

If h:[0,1]→R is continuous with h(0)=-2 and h(1)=3, then h([0,1]) is connected and hence an interval containing -2 and 3. Therefore 0∈h([0,1]), so h(c)=0 for some c∈[0,1].

Medium/hard paper-style synthesis

Let h:[a,b]→R be continuous and let y lie between h(a) and h(b). The interval [a,b] is connected. Hence h([a,b]) is connected, so it is an interval in R. Because it contains both endpoint values, it contains y. Thus h(c)=y for some c∈[a,b].

Graduated exam bridges

1. Foundation: Compute χ for a triangle filled by one face. Check: 3−3+1=1; this is older-priority material.

2. Exam style: Let f:[0,1]→[0,1] be continuous. Explain why f has a fixed point. Check: apply IVT to g(x)=f(x)−x; this remains a useful follow-on rather than the exact 2025/26 question.

Hard paper-style synthesis

The role of surjectivity in the preservation proof must be explicit. If Y=U∪V is a separation and f:X→Y is onto, then f-1(U) and f-1(V) are both nonempty and cover X. Continuity makes them open, so they would separate connected X.

Practice question - connected images and IVT [6 marks]

Inspired by: MA342 2025/26 Q4(b). Task. (a) Let f:X→Y be a continuous surjection. Show that connectedness of X implies connectedness of Y. (b) Briefly explain how this result implies the Intermediate Value Theorem. [6 marks]

Demand diagnosis and fastest route: pull a hypothetical separation of Y back to X, then apply the theorem to a continuous real function on an interval.

Worked answer: Suppose Y=U∪V were a separation. Continuity makes f-1(U) and f-1(V) open; surjectivity makes them nonempty and ensures their union is X. They are disjoint, contradicting connectedness of X. Hence Y is connected. For IVT, let h:[a,b]→R be continuous. The interval [a,b] is connected, so h([a,b]) is connected and therefore an interval in R. Since it contains h(a) and h(b), it contains every number between them, which is precisely IVT.

Topic-specific trap: continuity alone does not make both preimages nonempty; surjectivity is used there.

Mistakes

  • Counting a shared edge twice in a triangulation.
  • Applying Brouwer when the map does not send the closed ball to itself.
  • Spending core-revision time on older applications without current lecture evidence.
  • Calling h([a,b]) an interval without first establishing connectedness.
  • Recovery rule: Euler's formula uses faces of a particular planar embedding and needs the connected-version constant 2; adjust for disconnected graphs.

Checklist

  • I can compute V−E+F for a small complex.
  • I can derive IVT from connected continuous images.
  • I can state the fixed-point hypothesis and conclusion.
  • I have completed the eight core guides before this sheet.
  • Final 60-second audit: Hypotheses, incidence count, algebraic rearrangement and structural conclusion are all justified.

Past-paper note

Split confidence: the connected-image/IVT bridge is now high-confidence current material because it appears directly in 2025/26 Q4(b). Euler, triangulation, Brouwer, FTA and Nash remain low-confidence: they occur in 2018–2022/23 but are absent from all three papers in the 2023/24–2025/26 format. Back to paper evidence.
